title: Short Stuff: Arctic Fox
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Arctic fox. The hosts cover its small size and weight range, Arctic range, and cold adaptations: a compact body shape, the warmest coat of any Arctic animal with a trapped insulating air layer, a fluffy tail used as a face covering, hair on footpads, countercurrent blood circulation, and a slower winter metabolism. They discuss the blue (gray-blue) color variety, poor suitability as pets (smell, difficulty training, illegality in some places), diet (omnivorous but mostly meat, following polar bears for scraps), hunting by hearing prey under snow and pouncing, and breeding (litters of about twenty kits born dark, weaning around 45 days, independence within about six to ten months, lifespan in captivity up to sixteen years and roughly eight in the wild). Near the end they digress into recommending the TV series The Terror and talk about the show The Leftovers. Includes a sponsor mention and sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to Arctic fox
segments.summary: Hosts joke around about gray hair and a Detroit show inside joke, then introduce the Arctic fox as small, cute, and able to survive harsh Arctic conditions.

segments.title: Size, range and cold survival adaptations
segments.summary: Arctic foxes range from chihuahua-sized to jack russell-sized, up to about eight pounds, and live in circumpolar areas where temperatures fall to about negative 50 Celsius. Discussion covers compact body shape and small ears, the warmest coat of any Arctic animal with trapped warm air, a fluffy tail used as a face covering, hair on footpads, countercurrent blood circulation, and a slower winter metabolism. A brief aside recalls Simo Hayha, the White Death.

segments.title: Blue color variety
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the blue Arctic fox color variety, which is more of a gray-blue, and note that online photos may be altered.

segments.title: Arctic foxes as pets
segments.summary: Some people in Arctic areas keep them as pets, but the hosts say they make poor pets: they smell like skunk-like urine, are hard to train, and keeping them in warm southern places is cruel and illegal in some places.

segments.title: Diet and hunting
segments.summary: Arctic foxes are technically omnivores though they prefer meat and will eat seaweed and berries when food is scarce. They store body fat for winter and follow polar bears to scavenge scraps. Their wide, short ears let them hear prey under snow, and they pounce through the snow to catch it year round.

segments.title: Breeding, young, and lifespan
segments.summary: Females (vixens) give birth once a year in spring to early summer, typically around twenty dark-born kits, which are weaned at about forty-five days and sometimes helped by siblings. Young leave within six to ten months and mature around nine to ten months. Captive lifespan reaches up to about sixteen years, and wild lifespan is likely around eight years.

segments.title: Tangent: The Terror and The Leftovers
segments.summary: The hosts digress into TV recommendations. They praise The Terror, an AMC anthology series about a lost polar expedition, available on Hulu, and then discuss finishing season one of The Leftovers.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode, thank the Arctic fox, and note the show is an iHeartRadio production.
